'''Izak''' "'''Ieke'''" '''Moerdijk''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈikə ˈmuːrdɛik|lang}}; born 23 January 1958) is a Dutch mathematician, currently working at [[Utrecht University]], who in 2012 won the [[Spinoza Prize]].<ref name="www.nwo.nl">{{Cite web|title=NWO Spinoza Prize 2012 {{!}} NWO|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/nwo-spinoza-prize-2012|access-date=28 March 2021|website=www.nwo.nl|language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Moerdijk studied mathematics, philosophy and general linguistics at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. He obtained his PhD ''cum laude'' in 1985 at the same institution. His thesis was entitled ''Topics in intuitionism and topos theory'' and was written under the supervision of [[Anne Sjerp Troelstra]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Album Academicum|url=https://albumacademicum.uva.nl/id/id051942|access-date=28 March 2021|website=albumacademicum.uva.nl}}</ref><ref name="Ieke Moerdijk">{{Cite web|title=Ieke Moerdijk – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=55506|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref>

After that, he worked as [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of Chicago]] and [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]]. From 1988 to 2011 he was professor at [[Utrecht University]]. After working at the Mathematical Institute of the [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] for a few years, he returned to [[Utrecht University]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Catalogus Professorum – Prof Detail|url=https://profs.library.uu.nl/index.php/profrec/getprofdata/1404/44/71/0|access-date=28 March 2021|website=profs.library.uu.nl}}</ref>

In 2000 Moerdijk was an invited speaker to the 3rd [[European Congress of Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Parallel Lectures|url=http://www.imub.ub.edu/3ecm/parallel.htm|access-date=28 March 2021|website=www.imub.ub.edu}}</ref> He was elected member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2006<ref>{{cite web|author=|date=|title=Ieke Moerdijk|url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/5269|access-date=30 June 2015|publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|language=Dutch}}</ref> and of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Academy of Europe: Moerdijk Izak|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Moerdijk_Izak|access-date=28 March 2021|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

Moerdijk received the 2011 [[Descartes-Huygens Prize|Descartes-Huygens prize]] for his contribution to French–Dutch scientific collaborations from the [[Académie des sciences|Académie des Sciences]] in Paris.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Remise du prix Descartes-Huygens 2012|work=[[Académie des sciences]]|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/presse/communique/prixdescartes_190312.pdf|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Descartes-Huygens Prize for François Hammer and Ieke Moerdijk — KNAW|url=https://knaw.nl/en/news/news/descarteshuygensprijsvoorfranassoishammer|access-date=28 March 2021|website=knaw.nl|archive-date=21 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421131039/https://www.knaw.nl/en/news/news/descarteshuygensprijsvoorfranassoishammer|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012 he received the [[Spinoza Prize|Spinoza prize]] from the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]].<ref name="www.nwo.nl" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Spinoza Prize for Ieke Moerdijk of Radboud University Nijmegen (€2.5 million)|url=https://www.ru.nl/phd/research/prizes-achievements/spinoza-prize-winners/more-info/spinoza-prize-ieke-moerdijk-radboud-university/|access-date=28 March 2021|website=Information for PhD candidates|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Dutch Mathematician Ieke Moerdjik wins the Spinoza Prize {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/news/12/06/30/dutch-mathematician-ieke-moerdjik-wins-spinoza-prize|access-date=28 March 2021|website=euro-math-soc.eu}}</ref>

== Research ==
Moerdijk's research interests lie in the fields of [[category theory]], [[Algebraic topology|algebraic]] and [[differential topology]], and their applications to [[mathematical logic]].

Moerdijk is seen, together with [[André Joyal]], as one of the founders of algebraic set theory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=algebraic set theory in nLab|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/algebraic+set+theory|access-date=28 March 2021|website=ncatlab.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Joyal|first1=Andri|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/algebraic-set-theory/31FB231402C980AAEBAC0A02CB5F6DD9|title=Algebraic Set Theory|last2=Moerdijk|first2=Ieke|date=1995|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-55830-3|series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series|location=Cambridge|doi=10.1017/cbo9780511752483}}</ref> In 1992 he wrote, together with [[Saunders Mac Lane]], a book on [[topos theory]] that became the standard reference on the subject: ''Sheaves in geometry and logic. A first introduction to topos theory''.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Mac Lane|first1=Saunders|url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4612-0927-0|title=Sheaves in Geometry and Logic: A First Introduction to Topos Theory|last2=Moerdijk|first2=Ieke|date=1994|publisher=Springer New York|isbn=978-0-387-97710-2|series=Universitext|location=New York, NY|doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-0927-0}}</ref> In 1995 he made pioneering contributions to [[Constructive nonstandard analysis|constructive non-standard analysis]], of which he is one of the founders.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=16 May 1995|title=A model for intuitionistic non-standard arithmetic|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016%2F0168-0072%2893%29E0071-U|journal=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic|language=en|volume=73|issue=1|pages=37–51|doi=10.1016/0168-0072(93)E0071-U|issn=0168-0072|hdl=2066/129065|hdl-access=free|last1=Moerdijk|first1=Ieke|s2cid=11659129 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Moerdijk's research has also covered topics in [[differential geometry]]; in particular, he wrote in 2003 an influential monograph on [[foliation]]s and [[Lie groupoid]]s.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Moerdijk|first1=I.|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/introduction-to-foliations-and-lie-groupoids/75BBFED277FF39A56594731202789016|title=Introduction to Foliations and Lie Groupoids|last2=Mrcun|first2=J.|date=2003|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-83197-0|series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics|location=Cambridge|doi=10.1017/cbo9780511615450}}</ref> Recently Moerdijk pursues, among other topics, research on the theory of [[operad]]s, on the logic structure of [[quantum information theory]], and on [[Dendroidal set|dendroidal sets.]]

Moerdijk has written more than a hundred publications and is the author of several influential books. He supervised 19 PhD students as of 2021.<ref name="Ieke Moerdijk" />

==Selected books==
*Joyal, André; Moerdijk, Ieke (1995) ''Algebraic set theory''. [[London Mathematical Society]] Lecture Note Series, 220. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge. {{ISBN|978-0-511-75248-3}}
* Mac Lane, Saunders; Moerdijk, Ieke (1994) ''Sheaves in geometry and logic. A first introduction to topos theory''. Corrected reprint of the 1992 edition. Universitext. Springer-Verlag, New York, 1994. {{ISBN|978-0-387-97710-2}}
*Moerdijk, Ieke.; Mrčun, Janez (2003) ''Introduction to foliations and Lie groupoids''. Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics, 91. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge. {{ISBN|978-0-511-61545-0}}
*Moerdijk, Ieke; Reyes, Gonzalo E. (1991) ''Models for smooth infinitesimal analysis''. Springer-Verlag, New York. {{ISBN|978-0-387-97489-7|}}
*Moerdijk, Ieke, ''Classifying spaces and classifying topoi'', [[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]] 1616, Springer 1995. vi+94 pp. {{ISBN|978-3-540-60319-1}}
{{commons category|Ieke Moerdijk}}
*Moerdijk, Ieke; Van Oosten, Jaap. (2018) ''Sets, models and proofs''. Springer Nature Switzerland, Cham. {{ISBN|978-3-319-92414-4}}
